questions.q: Why is running your training as a job better than rerunning a notebook by hand?
options: Jobs are always faster than notebooks on the same machine
A job records the code snapshot, environment, compute and inputs explicitly, and can run unattended and be rerun or compared
Notebooks cannot import scikit-learn in Azure ML
Jobs do not need an environment
questions.explain: Notebooks carry hidden state and undocumented dependencies. A job records what ran and with what, and executes on managed compute without you.

questions.q: To run cells in a studio notebook you need which two things?
options: A running compute instance and a kernel (for example the SDK v2 kernel)
A Key Vault and a container registry
An mltable and a datastore URI
A compute cluster with min_instances=0 and a Docker image
questions.explain: The notebook toolbar attaches to a compute instance and a kernel. Clusters are for jobs, not interactive cells.

questions.q: In a command job, what does ${{inputs.data}} inside the command string represent?
options: A Python f-string evaluated on your laptop
A secret stored in Key Vault
A placeholder that the service replaces with the path of the input named data
The name of the compute cluster
questions.explain: Inputs are declared in the inputs dictionary and referenced in the command with the ${{inputs.<name>}} expression.

questions.q: What happens if you omit the compute argument when you create a command job?
options: The job fails validation
The job runs on your local machine
A compute instance is created for you and left running
Serverless compute is used
questions.explain: Per the Microsoft docs, leaving out compute on a command job runs it on serverless compute.

questions.q: In this lesson, the local 'mimic' run of train.py printed accuracy=0.765 on the churn data. What does that demonstrate?
options: That the script is ready for production
The script is plain Python and can be tested outside Azure before submitting it as a job
That Azure ML would produce the identical number in the cloud on any package versions
That the churn data is real customer data
questions.explain: The script has nothing Azure-specific in it, so test it locally first. The data is illustrative, and cloud results depend on the environment and data actually used.
